exposure: demographics (age, place of birth, CALD status)
background medical and pregnancy histories (previous cesarean section, pre-existing co-morbidity, previous miscarriage)
outcome: outcome of current pregnancy (miscarriage, viable pregnancy, ectopic, molar pregnancy)
cohort: The study analyzed data from 966 women who were seen in the Early Pregnancy Assessment Service (EPAS) at Liverpool Hospital, NSW, over a one-year period from January 1, 2018, to December 31, 2018, presenting with pain and/or vaginal bleeding in early pregnancy.
finding: Treatment via the Early Pregnancy Assessment Service (EPAS) is effective, with 86% success for conservative/medical management, but it requires significant time for assessment and follow-up visits depending on the gestation at presentation and the management option chosen.
gest_age: Gestational age at presentation to EPAS was predominantly 9 (7-10) weeks, and mostly 10 (7-12) weeks for women presenting with vaginal bleeding.
